In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the MAGE-A10 gene encodes for a tumor-associated Ag recognized by a CTL clone derived from a melanoma MLTC.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have generated a CTL line from patient LB1751 by stimulation of the patient's lymphocytes with autologous tumor cell lines.
we have identified a tumor-specific Ag, which is expressed on many melanomas and is recognized by CTL, that may be useful in immunotherapy.
we have shown that the MAGE-3 gene is expressed in a melanoma cell line (LB1751), and that a cytolytic T cell line (LBCL-1) can be generated against LB1751 cells by MLTC.
The main takeaway from our work is that
CTL clones can be generated from patients with melanoma using MLTC.
CTLs can be generated by autologous MLTC against a tumor cell line expressing a MAGE gene.
CTL clones can be generated by MLTC from melanoma patients that are able to recognize MAGE-A10, a gene that is frequently expressed by melanomas.
